items.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: I made it for a guy named Perry, Perry Bradford I think or something like that.

ctx.x: Now you made your first recording in 1924? © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

No, I made my first recording in Philadelphia way before that. But I, myself have never heard it. I made it for a guy named Perry, Perry Bradford I think or something like that. I can’t, I forget his name a little bit. He was a kind of pioneer in recording in those days. He recorded the famous Mamie Smith, see that’s what I’m talking about, in that period.
Black Swan Records? He was with Black Swan?

items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: He asked me to do it and I did it, that's all, finished. He paid and that's all.

ctx.x: Well, when you were with Mamie Smith, do you remember yourself subbing for somebody should have been in the band, maybe it was the band coming from New York?
I don't know, I don't remember, see. I don't remember, see, exactly. See, because I, I think some Perry, that's why I keep on bringin' his name up - he asked me -
